question: Patient is taken up for CS at full dilatation. During the procedure, the surgeon encountered difficulty in delivering the deeply impacted fetal head. What is the best method employed in such situations?
explanation: Impaction of the fetal head can leave a lack of space for the operator to insert their hand anteriorly between the fetal head and pubic symphysis, hindering the standard approach to deliver the head at caesarean birth (CB). Abdominal cephalic disimpaction (using the dominant or non-dominant hand to flex and lift the baby's head upwards into the maternal abdomen) is likely to be effective in the majority of cases of impacted fetal head (IFH) at CB. If the obstetrician is unable to disimpact the head with these standard manoeuvres, several strategies can be employed, including tocolysis, vaginal disimpaction (push-up), reverse breech extraction and the Patwardhan method. There is a lack of consensus regarding which technique is safest or most effective. Non-recommended techniques: a single forceps blade or ventouse used abdominally, or bladder filling, are not supported by evidence; use of a vacuum at CB can cause significant fetal injury (intracranial and subgaleal haemorrhage) and should be avoided. The algorithm for IFH at caesarean section summarises anticipate and prepare, diagnose IFH, declare the emergency, call for help, pause, consider tocolysis, abdominal cephalic disimpaction (A), consider changing hands, then vaginal disimpaction (B) or reverse breech extraction (C), and repeating the above or considering the Patwardhan manoeuvre.
